provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: God answers prayers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what prayer is.
The pupils should be able to explain that God answers prayers.

Introduction:
We pray to God every day.
Today we learn about Hannah and her prayer.

Content:
Hannah prayed for a child.
God heard her prayer.
God gave her a baby boy named Samuel.
We can pray like Hannah.
God hears all our prayers.

Class activity:
Let us all pray together for our families.

Evaluation questions:
What is prayer?
Did God answer Hannah's prayer?
Can God hear your prayers?

Summary:
God answers our prayers when we pray to Him.

topics.title: Jesus helps the sick
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sick people.
The pupils should be able to explain that Jesus helps the sick.

Introduction:
Sometimes we feel sick.
Today we learn how Jesus helps sick people.

Content:
Jesus saw many sick people.
Jesus touched them and healed them.
The sick people felt better.
Jesus cares for us when we are sick.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to be sick and then pretend Jesus heals us.

Evaluation questions:
What happens when people are sick?
Who helps sick people?
How does Jesus help the sick?

Summary:
Jesus helps sick people because He cares for them.

topics.title: Jesus feeds the people
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of Jesus feeding the people.
The pupils should be able to explain that God provides.

Introduction:
We all need food to eat.
Today we learn about a time Jesus fed many people.

Content:
Jesus had five loaves of bread.
Jesus had two small fish.
Jesus prayed and shared the food.
Five thousand people ate and were full.
God can provide with little.

Class activity:
Let us count our fingers and pretend to share food.

Evaluation questions:
How many loaves did Jesus have?
How many people ate the food?
What did Jesus teach us about sharing?

Summary:
God provides for our needs when we trust Him.

topics.title: Telling the truth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define truth.
The pupils should be able to explain why God loves truth.

Introduction:
We must always tell the truth.
Today we learn about truthful children.

Content:
A truthful child says what is real.
A truthful child does not lie.
God loves children who tell the truth.
God is happy when we are truthful.

Class activity:
Let us practice saying the truth about our favorite colors.

Evaluation questions:
What is truth?
Why should we tell the truth?
Does God love truthful children?

Summary:
God loves us when we tell the truth.

topics.title: The honest boy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of Joseph.
The pupils should be able to explain that honesty pays.

Introduction:
Joseph was an honest boy.
Today we learn about his story.

Content:
Joseph was sold to Egypt.
Joseph worked hard and was honest.
Joseph became a leader in Egypt.
God blessed Joseph because he was honest.
Honesty always brings good things.

Class activity:
Let us act the story of Joseph being sold to Egypt.

Evaluation questions:
Who was Joseph?
What did Joseph do that was good?
What happened to Joseph because he was honest?

Summary:
God rewards honest people like Joseph.

topics.title: Helping the needy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify people who need help.
The pupils should be able to explain ways to help others.

Introduction:
Some people need our help.
Today we learn about Dorcas who helped people.

Content:
Dorcas helped poor people.
Dorcas made clothes for them.
Dorcas was kind to everyone.
We can help people like Dorcas.

Class activity:
Let us draw clothes to give to poor people.

Evaluation questions:
Who was Dorcas?
What did Dorcas do to help people?
How can you help someone in need?

Summary:
We should help people who need our help.

topics.title: God made me to praise Him
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what praise is.
The pupils should be able to praise God with songs.

Introduction:
We should thank God for making us.
Today we learn how to praise God.

Content:
Praise means to thank and worship God.
God made us to praise Him.
We can praise God with songs.
We can praise God with our words.

Class activity:
Let us sing praise songs together.

Evaluation questions:
What is praise?
Why did God make us?
How can we praise God?

Summary:
We should praise God every day for making us.

topics.title: God keeps me safe
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of Daniel.
The pupils should be able to explain that God protects us.

Introduction:\Sometimes we are in danger.
Today we learn how God protected Daniel.

Content:
Daniel was in a den with lions.
God sent an angel to protect Daniel.
The lions did not hurt Daniel.
God protects us from danger.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to be lions and then pretend God protects us.

Evaluation questions:
What happened to Daniel?
Who protected Daniel?
How does God protect us?

Summary:
God keeps us safe from all harm.

topics.title: The happy home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to describe a God fearing home.
The pupils should be able to explain how to have peace at home.

Introduction:
Our home should be a happy place.
Today we learn about God fearing homes.

Content:
A God fearing home prays together.
A God fearing home loves each other.
A God fearing home has peace.
God blesses homes that fear Him.

Class activity:
Let us draw our happy homes.

Evaluation questions:
What is a God fearing home?
How can we have peace at home?
Why should we love our family?

Summary:
God gives peace to homes that love Him.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall stories learned.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about the term's work.

Introduction:
We have learned many stories this term.
Today we will revise and be assessed.

Content:
We learned about prayer and God's answers.
We learned about Jesus helping the sick.
We learned about honesty and helping others.
We learned about praising God.

Class activity:
Let us sing praise songs and tell stories.

Evaluation questions:
Tell one thing you learned about prayer.
How does Jesus help us?
Why is it important to tell the truth?

Summary:
We remember all we learned this term.
